title: lwb Proof of Completion record
description: Owner directive 7: Proof of Completion on every deliverable; done = committed AND pushed with a proof record and green CI. See proof/README.md.

deliverable.description: The deliverable's id, e.g. an issue/step number or a short slug.

pr.description: The PR number this record proves. Optional in the schema, but it is the ONLY thing the directive-7 gates key on, both pre-merge (lwb-proof-pr) and post-merge (lwb-proof-coverage) -- the squash-merge commit does not exist while a PR's own CI runs, so 'commit' cannot be matched pre-merge. Do NOT reintroduce a fallback onto 'deliverable': a deliverable is documented below as an issue/step number or a slug, so a small integer there is ordinary usage, and accepting it as a PR alias let a record for step 6 of an unrelated plan silently satisfy PR #6's gate. See scripts/lwb_check_proof.py::check_pr_has_record.

author.description: Identity of whoever did the work (a session/dispatch id, not just 'claude' or 'codex').

checked_by.description: Identity of whoever independently checked it. Must differ from 'author' — see the schema-level check in scripts/lwb_check_proof.py.

commit.description: The commit SHA this proof record proves.

argv.description: The exact command run, as an argv list (no shell string — avoids a shell-quoting ambiguity in the proof record itself).

expect_exit.description: The exit code this command was expected to produce.

tail.description: At most the last 10 lines of the command's combined output.

sha256.description: sha256 of the command's full captured output (stdout+stderr concatenated), so a 10-line tail can't quietly hide a truncated failure — see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py's re-hash check.

sanitiser_version.description: scripts/lwb_sanitise.py's SANITISER_VERSION at the time this command's output was sanitised, so the digest is attributable to a known set of substitution rules rather than to whichever throwaway script a session happened to hand-write that day. Required, and enforced, for records from PR #20 onward (docs/maintainers/proof-of-completion-plan.md, open blocker 1); records 7-19 predate scripts/lwb_sanitise.py entirely and are not backfilled.

verifiable.description: Whether this exact command is independently re-executable by CI on a fresh checkout. Measured, not assumed -- docs/maintainers/proof-of-completion-plan.md counts the distinct command kinds found across proof/*.json and finds five re-execute cleanly, three cannot (e.g. wall-clock/terminal-width-dependent output, or a symbolic git range CI cannot reproduce), and two are conditional (need a repo secret or a gitignored build step). Required, and enforced, for records from PR #20 onward; see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py.

verifiable_reason.description: Required when 'verifiable' is false. A CLOSED enum, machine-checked -- free text is an advisory rule, and a reason a validator cannot check is not a check. See the plan's measured table for which command kinds take which reason.

resolved_base.description: For a command whose argv names a git revision range (a single 'a..b' token, or separate --base/--head flags) -- the actual sha this command's 'base' side resolved to when it was run. Without this, CI substituting the symbolic argv (e.g. origin/main..HEAD) resolves a DIFFERENT commit than the one the record proves, and an honest record fails -- open blocker 3.

resolved_head.description: As resolved_base, for the 'head' side of a git revision range.

mutations.description: Every file this deliverable's work created or changed, repo-relative path.

unproven.description: Anything claimed as part of this deliverable that this record does NOT prove (an honest gap list, not a place to hide a failure as a footnote).

acceptance_criteria.description: What 'done' meant for this deliverable, agreed before the work started; quality floor item 1. Each entry is a criterion and whether it was met -- required, and enforced, for records from PR #12 onward; see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py.

tokens.description: Measured token cost, per the mission's efficiency section: total input, cached input, uncached input, output, retries, setup overhead, tool overhead and wall time, separately, plus where the numbers came from. A field that cannot be measured is recorded as the string "unknown", NEVER as zero -- an unmeasured field recorded as zero is exactly how an efficiency claim gets manufactured. Instruction-length proxies are not billed tokens. Required, and enforced, for records from PR #12 onward; see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py. `total_input`, `cached_input`, `uncached_input`, `output` and `wall_time_seconds` come from a session transcript's `message.usage` blocks (type:"assistant" records) at `~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/<session_id>.jsonl`: `total_input` is `usage.input_tokens` plus both cache fields, `cached_input` is `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` + `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`, `uncached_input` is `usage.input_tokens` alone, `output` is `usage.output_tokens` (with an `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` sub-split), and `wall_time_seconds` is the difference between the transcript's first and last ISO8601 `timestamp`. `retries`, `setup_overhead` and `tool_overhead` have no source on any current runtime -- confirmed against Claude Code's own `SubagentStop` hook payload and a real transcript's field set -- and are expected to be recorded as "unknown". Two structural limits bound any efficiency claim built from this field: usage attaches per MODEL TURN, not per tool call, so one usage block covers every tool call in that turn and tokens can never be attributed to an individual tool call; and subagent transcripts are frequently deleted before SubagentStop fires, so subagent spend capture is lossy in practice -- a missing subagent cost is "unknown", not zero.

source.description: Where these numbers came from. Must START WITH (anchored, no leading whitespace) one of exactly two origins re-derivable from a FRESH CLONE on a machine that never had any particular plugin installed: "transcript message.usage" (the numeric fields were read from a session transcript's `message.usage` blocks, as described above) or "unknown" (no measurement was possible). Detail may follow the origin -- a colon, a parenthetical, derivation notes such as which file and how many records were summed -- that is honest provenance, not noise, and is expected. A string that does not START WITH one of those two origins, including a script name like "spend-ledger" from a plugin the owner is removing, cites a source nobody can re-derive and is rejected -- see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py::_validate_tokens.
